meath/transportation-urban-regeneration/.quote: MB referred Item to the next SPC in order to facilitate attendance of Cllr. Helen Meyer who could not attend due to other commitments.
It was agreed to be reviewed on assessment of the maps with the “red “roads.
It was agreed that the SPC should continue to work towards developing a practical approach, with the aim of putting an alternative method in place.
Members agreed that glyphosate is a harmful product and that having further detailed information would be beneficial in progressing the discussion.
Following discussion, members agreed that the proposal should be considered at a county-wide policy level in line with the remit of the SPC.
It was agreed to investigate how a pilot scheme could operate on a county-wide basis, rather than being limited to a specific Municipal District.
Acceptance of the Terms of Reference as presented was proposed by AS and seconded by SD.

Agenda Items agreed are as follows: Transportation Minutes of Previous Meeting Matters Arising from Minutes Agenda Items referred to the SPC through the Full Council or MD Meetings The Roadworks Programme Road Safety initiatives / Traffic Calming Measures Winter gritting Programme Active Travel Public Transport Navan Rail Line Roads & Sustainable Transport Schemes Public Lighting Urban Regeneration Update from the Regeneration Team – Ongoing Projects Correspondence & Circulars AOB
It was agreed that subsequent meetings would be as follows: Thursday 22nd May @ 2.30pm Thursday 11th September @ 2.30pm Thursday 20th November @ 2.30pm
Cllr Sean Drew (SD) was proposed as Acting Chair by Cllr Paddy Meade and Seconded by Cllr Amanda Smith (AS).
The committee agreed in principle to commence the process.
Acceptance of the Footpath extension Programme was agreed by the Committee.
It was agreed to seek a budget allocation, subject to the SPC returning their comments by 25th September 2025, to allow us to bring the draft Policy to the MDs and the Plenary.
If funding becomes available, acceptance of the Community Centers Footpath Programme was agreed by the members.
Meath County Council Traffic Calming Policy was adopted by the Plenary Council on 3rd November 2025 and is available online on www.meath.ie.
